answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because ocean only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, velvet is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
